why_this_file: Any single contested choice in a valuation is defensible. What is not is a study that resolves EVERY contested choice the same way and never notices — which is how a lean survives an audit of its steps. Each is recorded with BOTH framings' values, the side adopted and why, and the binomial sign test is printed. A study landing them all one way is FLAGGED, never failed: a company can genuinely deserve a consistent read, and a gate that failed on it would push studies to resolve judgements inconsistently to stay green.
both_framings_share_a_bridge: Every alternative is computed by RE-RUNNING this study's own compute.py with that one choice changed and everything else held at its published value, through the same lenses and the same bridge as the adopted figure — so the difference measures the CHOICE and not the construction. Each source substitution is asserted to have landed exactly once, and the re-run is proved against the committed answer before any alternative is believed.
the_answer_this_record_is_anchored_on: This study publishes TWO branches and no single figure. Every row is valued on Frame A, the branch the shared reader resolves, with the Frame B pair recorded beside it; the two move together on every row except the inventory judgement itself, which IS the difference between the branches.
materiality: A judgement is material where the two framings differ by more than 5% of value. Because the published answer is a weighted centre of four lenses, a driver change moves it LESS than it moves the cash-flow lens alone — which is a real property of the published construction and not a softening of the test; the cash-flow-lens effect is larger on every row that touches a driver.

judgements.name: the central: the four-lens weighted blend vs the class primary alone
judgements.adopted: a weighted centre — cash flow 40%, normalised earnings 25%, relative multiple 20%, book and sustainable return 15%
judgements.alternative: the cash-flow lens alone as the central, the others published beside it as cross-checks
judgements.direction: the study adopted the lower-value framing
judgements.why: [R-LENS-03] retires the typed blend: one class primary IS the central, the other lenses are cross-checks, and book value is a disclosed floor that is never weighted. Three of the four weighted lenses here value the company on reported accounting earnings and historical-cost book, and the weights never cleared an out-of-sample test. This is the study's largest contested construction and it is on that rule's ratchet until the study is rebuilt; the alternative is the study's own cash-flow reading, unchanged, not a new model.

judgements.name: the FY2026 commercial margin per litre: a +17.0% step vs the 2.0% escalator the retail leg takes
judgements.adopted: a 17.0% step in FY2026, described as the realised first-half outcome
judgements.alternative: the same 2.0% domestic escalator the retail margin per litre takes
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: The step is applied TO the realised first half — the commercial margin per litre is anchored on the disclosed half-year figure and the escalator then multiplies it — so the realised outcome is the anchor rather than the case for the step, and that anchor is already 19.2% above the prior-year half on the company's own disclosure. The company's own quarterly figures have underlying EBITDA falling from USD 305mn in the first quarter to USD 298mn in the second. A harsher reading still, holding the margin flat at the realised half with no FY2026 step at all, gives AED 4.0584.

judgements.name: terminal growth: a typed nominal 1.50% vs the house AE terminal of 2.00% at zero real growth
judgements.adopted: 1.50% nominal, set below the domestic escalator for the electric-vehicle drag
judgements.alternative: 2.00% nominal, the house AE terminal inflation at zero real growth
judgements.direction: the study adopted the lower-value framing
judgements.why: [R-MACRO-01] stores a growth rate as (real, inflation path) and recomputes the nominal. A typed 1.50% against a terminal inflation of 2.00% is a real decline of 0.490% a year in perpetuity — which may well be right for a fuel retailer facing the transition this study models, and which the study nowhere writes down as the real number it is. The alternative is the house path's own terminal, not a view.

judgements.name: country risk: a 4bp market default spread stripped against a 64bp rating premium added back, vs the rating basis on both sides
judgements.adopted: strip the 4bp spread the July-2026 dirham auction actually contains, add back the 64bp rating-based country premium
judgements.alternative: the rating basis on both sides — strip the 42bp rating default spread, add back the same 64bp premium
judgements.direction: the study adopted the lower-value framing
judgements.why: Country risk must enter exactly once and the SAME basis must be stripped as is added back. The study strips a market-observed 4bp and adds back a rating-based 64bp, and gives its reason in its own record: removing 42bp from a bond that carries 4bp puts the normalised rate below the matched-tenor Treasury under a hard peg, which cannot be right. The reason is good and the bases still do not match, so both are priced. The consistent-basis reading lowers the normalised risk-free rate by 38bp and the cost of equity with it.

judgements.name: the justified multiple's payout: derived from the sustainable-growth identity vs the company's own 75% policy floor
judgements.adopted: payout = 1 - g/ROE, so the multiple satisfies g = retention x return
judgements.alternative: the 75% of net profit the dividend policy actually commits to
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: Both are defensible and they are not the same question. The identity keeps the multiple internally consistent — at a sustainable return on equity of 80.8% a 75% payout implies growth far above the 1.5% the same multiple capitalises — and it removes the free parameter the critiques objected to. The company's disclosed commitment is nonetheless 75% of net profit or USD 700mn if higher, and the board paid the floor rather than a share of the spiked half-year profit. Adopting the identity raises the payout the multiple uses to 98.1% and raises the value.

judgements.name: tax: the audited FY2025 effective rate of 10.17% vs the 15% domestic minimum top-up
judgements.adopted: 10.17%, the rate the audited FY2025 reconciliation actually shows
judgements.alternative: 15%, the domestic minimum top-up rate in force for groups above the revenue threshold
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: The company is plainly within the size threshold and its own audited reconciliation does not apply the top-up; the reviewed half-year runs 10.09%. Following the filing rather than the reader's expectation of it is the source rule working. It is a risk rather than a defect, and it is the largest single identifiable downside construction the study itself names — the study prices it on its own cash-flow lens and this row carries it through every lens the rate touches, which is why the figure here is larger.

judgements.name: inventory movements: normalised to zero from FY2027 vs carried at the FY2024-FY2025 average
judgements.adopted: published BOTH ways and never averaged — Frame A and Frame B
judgements.direction: the study adopted the lower-value framing
judgements.why: The study takes no side and the dual framing is the right answer: inventory movements are not a line in the audited statements, appearing only in management commentary with no reconciliation to the accounts. The two branches are recorded here as the two framings so the fork is measured rather than exempted. The direction below is an artefact of anchoring this record on Frame A, which is the branch the shared reader resolves; the difference sits under the materiality bar at the published centre though it is 6.2% on the cash-flow lens alone.

judgements.name: the cost of capital: flat, vs the glide to a drifted beta and a 10% terminal debt weight
judgements.adopted: flat — today is the terminal under a hard peg, so the explicit and terminal rates are identical
judgements.alternative: the glide the delivered document still describes, with beta drifting 38.9% of the way to one and a 10% terminal debt weight
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: Flat is what the cost-of-capital procedure returns for a pegged market and it is the right construction. The retired glide is priced here because eight delivered passages still describe it, so a reader has been told the study does something it does not — a defect already on the study's own findings list. Adopting flat raises the value, and the alternative is what the document says is being done.

judgements.name: the relative lens's earnings year: FY2026, the inventory-gain peak, vs FY2027
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: FY2026 carries the AED 762mn realised inventory gain the company itself excludes from underlying EBITDA, and it is higher than FY2027, FY2028 and FY2029 operating profit, so a multiple applied to it capitalises the peak year. The lens was de-circularised when the price-derived legs were dropped; the year it is applied to was not revisited.

judgements.name: the reference multiple: the fundamentals-derived leg alone vs the three-leg average carrying the traded multiples
judgements.alternative: the average of the justified multiple, today's traded multiple and the own three-year mean
judgements.direction: the study adopted the lower-value framing
judgements.why: Two of the three legs are the traded price divided by earnings, so the three-leg average made a lens presented as independent evidence about value two-thirds a restatement of the price it was being compared against. Dropping them is right and it LOWERED the value; the alternative is what the first edition published.

judgements.name: the impairment and credit-loss charge: normalised down vs held at the annualised first half of 2026
judgements.adopted: FY2026 at the realised first half annualised, then a normalised level escalating with inflation
judgements.alternative: held at the annualised first-half rate for the whole window
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: FY2025 carried AED 284.3mn and the first half of 2026 AED 179.9mn, both described by the company as prudence-based provisioning. Calling the elevated level temporary is a judgement about a charge that has risen in each of the last two periods, and it is made in the direction that raises the value.

judgements.name: the terminal return on capital: faded to 25.0% vs the company's own disclosed FY2025 figure
judgements.adopted: 25.0%, fading the disclosed return toward a mature network
judgements.alternative: the return on capital employed the company itself disclosed for FY2025
judgements.direction: the study adopted the lower-value framing
judgements.why: The company disclosed 32.7% for FY2025 and 40.1% for the first half of 2026 on its own measure, and this study's own committed history computes 54.4% for FY2025 on the study's own definition. The fade is the conservative side and it costs value, because the terminal reinvestment charge is growth over return.

judgements.name: the sustainable return in the book lens: the three-year mean vs the latest audited year
judgements.adopted: the three-year mean of the return on equity attributable to shareholders
judgements.direction: the study adopted the lower-value framing
judgements.why: The return rose in each of the three audited years, so the mean (80.77%) sits below the latest reading (86.49%) and the mean is the lower of the two. The expert appendix names this as that lens's most sensitive input and runs it the other way, to the earliest year; this row runs it to the most recent.

judgements.name: capital spending: maintenance set equal to depreciation vs the realised FY2023-25 net rate
judgements.adopted: maintenance at the depreciation rate on the opening base, plus growth capital per station added
judgements.alternative: the mean realised FY2023-25 excess of capital spending over depreciation, held through the window
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: The steady-state condition that a network replaces what it consumes is the standard construction and it reconciles FY2026 to the company's own guidance. It is nonetheless below what this company has actually spent: capital spending exceeded depreciation by a mean of AED 387mn a year across the three audited years, against AED 220mn in the model's own first forecast year.

judgements.name: working capital: the related-party-inclusive cycle vs trade balances alone
judgements.adopted: the cycle as the audited balance sheet presents it, including balances with related parties
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: The study publishes both cycles and says which it uses and why: the related-party presentation is the balance sheet that exists. A reader who thinks those terms would not survive an arm's-length renegotiation should use the other, which the study also says. The adopted reading is the one that releases cash.

judgements.name: the minority: deducted at book vs at its share of equity value
judgements.alternative: its disclosed profit share of the equity value the model produces
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: [R-BRIDGE-01] deducts the minority at its share of value rather than at historical cost, because the model capitalises the whole of subsidiary cash flow. On the disclosed profit share of 2.0007% that is about AED 1,201mn against the AED 230.4mn book amount deducted. The book deduction is the smaller charge and the higher value.

judgements.name: leases: deducted in the bridge with right-of-use depreciation inside the charge, vs treated as operating
judgements.adopted: the lease liability deducted in the bridge, the rent not added back
judgements.alternative: rent charged in cash operating costs, the right-of-use asset out of the depreciable base, no lease deducted in the bridge
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: The study names this as contested and prices only the bridge leg, at AED 1,446mn or AED 0.12 a share. The alternative is priced here in full, which takes three coordinated changes rather than one plus a depreciation rate re-measured excluding right-of-use assets from the study's own committed figures (8.2750% against the committed 8.3600%); it is reported as a reconstruction for that reason. Mixing the two treatments would double-count, which is the study's own point.

judgements.name: the bridge: the audited 31-Dec-2025 sheet vs the reviewed 30-Jun-2026 sheet
judgements.alternative: the reviewed 30-June-2026 balance sheet, whose income statement the model already consumes
judgements.direction: the study adopted the higher-value framing
judgements.why: [R-BRIDGE-01] stands the bridge on the LATEST disclosed sheet. The reviewed interim is in this study's own source set and its income statement is fully consumed while its balance sheet is not. Net debt, leases and the minority all move, and the net effect is against the study's own answer. The three figures are read from that filing by this study's own gap review of 5 September and are not committed inputs of the model, which is why this row is the one alternative below that does not come from the committed register.

not_valued.name: the equity risk premium basis
not_valued.why_not: The published country-risk file carries a rating-based row for the UAE and no credit-default-swap-based row, so the second framing does not exist in the original source. Constructing one from a third-party quote that contradicts the original file would be worse than disclosing the gap, and the study says so. Reported unvalued rather than guessed.
not_valued.one_sided_price: the study offers a beta of 0.80 as arithmetically equivalent to a premium about forty per cent higher, worth AED 4.25 on its own cash-flow lens

not_valued.name: the proposed acquisition of Shell Downstream South Africa
not_valued.adopted: excluded from every number, and disclosed as excluded
not_valued.why_not: Announced on 7 July 2026 at approximately USD 1,000mn of enterprise value, after the 30 June sheet and not closed. No consideration structure, no funding split and no acquired earnings are disclosed, so the including framing cannot be built from the filings without inventing its terms. The exclusion is applied consistently on both sides of the bridge.

not_valued.name: the 45 fils per litre minimum margin under the parent supply agreement
not_valued.adopted: not carried as a driver; the retail margin per litre is built from the disclosed gross profit and litres
not_valued.why_not: The study's own negative-results record states that this figure — which it calls the single most consequential structural input — was sourced from secondary reporting of an exchange filing and never confirmed from the primary document. The model's own realised retail margin is about 36 fils, BELOW the quoted floor, so the two cannot be measuring the same thing; applying the floor as a forecast level would be inventing a driver on an unconfirmed source. Reported unvalued, and the delivered caption that calls 36.0 'comfortably above' 45 is a separate defect already on the study's own findings list.
not_valued.one_sided_price: not priced; the primary source was never obtained

not_treated_as_a_contested_judgement.name: beta
not_treated_as_a_contested_judgement.why: It is measured, not chosen: a five-year weekly regression against the published index of its own exchange, 257 observations, R-squared 0.179, usable on the gate, so no lower tier is reached for. The sensitivity table shows it is the largest single driver of value, which is a fact about the model rather than a fork the study resolved. The record's index file is registered under a filename the resolver does not carry, and that file is byte-identical to the one it does — a provenance defect on the study's own findings list, not a second framing of the number.

not_treated_as_a_contested_judgement.name: the dividend lens, flat versus grown
not_treated_as_a_contested_judgement.why: It carries no weight in either published centre, so both framings give the identical answer. It sets the bottom of the published range of readings and nothing else.
